name: codex
title: Codex / GPT cross-vendor interface
summary: Adds the OpenAI-backed half of the harness: the Sol reviewer as the default cross-family reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work through the Codex CLI, the harness's top executor rung (GPT-6 Astra at xhigh) plus a user-request-only Sol executor, both through the same CLI, and the two-architect /cross-compare-plan session (independent drafts, cross-critique, blind synthesis) whose GPT lane (Astra, xhigh effort) runs read-only through the same CLI.

bin: codex (Codex CLI) — for reviewer-codex, executor-codex-heavy, executor-codex-principal, and the cross-compare architect lane
env: OPENAI_API_KEY or `codex login` — review, execution, and cross-compare

notes: reviewer-codex is the default independent reviewer for Claude-authored campaign work; Codex-authored work goes to fresh-context Opus review instead. There is no reviewEngine switch. Docs-only work is exempt: a prose-only diff routes to fresh-context Opus review — no cross-family requirement, no alarm.

executor-codex-principal (GPT-6 Astra, xhigh) is the TOP RUNG OF THE HARNESS'S DEFAULT EXECUTOR LADDER, not a side lane: executor (Sonnet) then executor-heavy (Opus) then Astra, one rung per double bounce, so escalation crosses the vendor line at the top. Exceptional orders only, declared at PLAN time — never routine work, never a launcher's own escalation. Installing this pack therefore changes where escalated Claude work goes; without it the ladder has no top rung and the Director substitutes the Fable executor-principal, announced rather than silently.

executor-codex-heavy (GPT-5.6 Sol, high) is the cheaper cross-vendor executor and is USER REQUEST ONLY — no routing rule reaches it. It runs when the user names it, or when executorEngine: "codex" makes the Codex lane the project's executor lane.

Config keys (.claude/orchestra.json under "codex"): reviewModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), reviewTimeoutMs (default 2700000), execHeavyModel (default gpt-5.6-sol), execHeavyEffort (default high), execPrincipalModel (default gpt-6-astra), execPrincipalEffort (default xhigh), crossplanModel (default gpt-6-astra), crossplanEffort (default xhigh), engineMcp (default strip — every MCP server in the user's Codex config plus the apps connector is disabled for the engine child in every lane; inherit leaves it alone). Each executor rung reads only its own pair, so pinning one never moves the other; the heavy keys keep the names they shipped with.

Review is cross-family by default and that is the lane's first goal: Claude-authored work goes to reviewer-codex (Sol), Codex-authored work (an Astra or Sol executor's order) goes to the fresh-context Opus reviewer. The review runner strips the engine's MCP servers so it cannot delegate to a same-vendor review MCP, and stamps a verdict that names a Claude engine as its author with CROSS-FAMILY BREACH.

Windows: codex-command-runner.exe, codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe and codex-resources ship in the directory the install's own codex-package.json declares (resourcesDir, a sibling of bin\), and Codex resolves them from there. The self-check reads that manifest first and only then looks beside the binary. A hand copy into bin\ (or one directory down, inside bin\codex-resources\) is a stale kit from an older release and is the known cause of the intermittent sandbox fault. codex.helpersDir is a legacy escape hatch for a layout with no manifest; the runners never copy from it over helpers the manifest already carries.
Without this pack the harness still gets full fresh-context Opus review and Claude execution; it just has no cross-vendor option.
